title: DeMeco Ryans on Tank Dell, Defensive Fixes & Titans Week | Full Q&A
headline: Tank Dell, Braden Smith, and Kayden McDonald's practice windows open this week, so their Titans-week availability is the key fantasy watch; Kenneth Murray left Sunday with a concussion and no update was given.
summary: Ryans called the defense's struggles a technique and communication problem, not a scheme problem, and said the team has not done enough to earn a win. He stressed complementary football, citing special teams giving up explosives and a touchdown in the second half as a key failure. On offense he praised the game plan, the emphasis on winning first down, and C.J. Stroud's play, while saying the run blocking needs to finish better. He said the team expects to open the 21-day practice window this week for Tank Dell, Braden Smith, and Kayden McDonald, and that how they respond in practice will determine Sunday. He praised Kenneth Murray's preparation as the green-dot communicator but said Murray left the game with a concussion. Asked about the defense's bump-and-run usage for Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter, he said the team runs all those coverages without directly explaining the reduced press usage. He called penalties a mix of unavoidable bang-bang plays and controllable mistakes, citing pre-snap and alignment issues on special teams and offense. The next opponent is the Tennessee Titans.

title: Sean McVay, Byron Young & Kobie Turner discuss the Rams' Week 4 win over the Eagles, riding momentum into Monday Night Football & more
headline: Puka Nacua came out of the Eagles game feeling healthy, while Terrance Ferguson is on IR for at least four games and Aaron Donald is trending toward playing Monday against Buffalo.
summary: McVay said the Rams' Week 4 win at Philadelphia was built on late execution, even though the offense was inconsistent for much of the game. He credited the defense's fourth-down stop and its pressure for keeping the Rams in the game, and said the penalties and procedural mistakes need to be cleaned up. Puka Nacua was a key factor late, and McVay said he felt healthy after the game despite a hip concern raised by reporters. Aaron Donald is trending toward practicing and playing this week, though McVay would not commit. Terrance Ferguson was placed on IR for a medial ankle sprain, and McVay expects him back before season's end. McVay said Jaylen Watson's shoulder is improving and he is expected to be ready for Buffalo if practice goes well. On special teams, McVay called the return game and coverage inconsistent, with a costly long punt return and a missed field goal among the problems. The next game is Monday Night Football against the Bills, and McVay said the offense must play cleaner against Josh Allen's group.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Justin Herbert’s “Inspiring” Resilience
headline: Rashawn Slater (transcribed as "Sean") has a high ankle sprain and is a significant loss, possibly IR-bound; Joe Alt (neck) and Trevor Penning (concussion protocol) are still being evaluated.
summary: Harbaugh confirmed Rashawn Slater has a high ankle sprain and called his absence significant, with no timeline yet and IR possible. Joe Alt's neck injury is still being evaluated, and Harbaugh said Slater's situation looks more likely to become IR than Alt's. Trevor Penning is in the concussion protocol, and Donte Jackson has a hamstring issue. Harbaugh said Dalvin Tomlinson, Charlie Kolar and Brenen Thompson are making good progress, with another update coming Wednesday. Branson Taylor and Scott Matlock are expected to be activated from IR this week, while the status of another IR candidate is less certain. On the offensive line, rookies and Cole Strange and Jake Slaughter stepped in well, and Harbaugh's plan is next-man-up with a one-game-at-a-time approach. Harbaugh praised Justin Herbert's resilience and said it inspires the whole team, though he did not give a concrete answer about changes to the second-half checkdown approach. On the running backs, Harbaugh said he can't predict carry shares, all three backs are contributing, and Omarion Hampton is playing well despite a fumble.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 5, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley's hamstring injury leaves his Sunday availability uncertain. Sirianni will update on Wednesday.
summary: Sirianni said Saquon Barkley's availability for Sunday is still unknown after his hamstring injury, and that the team will have more answers by Wednesday as players respond to treatment. He said Barkley will do everything he can to return. On the offense, he said the team still hasn't settled on an identity, and the mix of under-center and gun sets reflects game-plan needs rather than a settled personnel decision. He acknowledged the goal-line and short-yardage failures (a fourth-and-one and a third-and-goal from the two) and said the tape review is about accountability and finding solutions. He gave no update on Lane Johnson's return. He praised rookie tackle Markel Bell's performance as solid, with good movement on double teams and second-level blocks, while noting he wasn't perfect. He said left guard Cam is doing good things and there is no plan to change him. On pass protection, he declined to say who makes the protection calls, called the breakdowns multiple factors including coaching and matchups, and said it has to be more consistent. He said the team will leave for the international trip on Friday to get a full week of practice in, and that jet lag was part of the planning.
